# dsh-visual-browser
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that gives the Agent a **real Chrome** and gives you a **live window into
it** — as a tab in the **right Sidebar**, right under the built-in *Browser* entry.

- The Agent never reads the DOM. It reads a numbered list of *visible interactive
elements* plus a s

hort text excerpt — a few hundred tokens per page instead of a
full DOM snapshot.
- **One tab strip

per workspace.** Sessions in the same workspace share the
strip and the Follow flag; another workspa

ce's pages are invisible (and
unaddressable) from here. `browser_open` puts a URL in a new tab of th

e
calling workspace.
- The tab streams Chrome's own screencast (CDP `Page.startScreencast`) as a
len

gth-prefixed JPEG stream, decoded off the main thread onto a canvas. No
screenshot polling, no per-f

rame request, no re-render of the panel per frame.
- Your pointer, wheel and keyboard go straight to

the DevTools input domain in
animation-frame batches: click, drag, scroll and type with normal late

ncy
instead of "screenshot after the fact" latency.
- The bottom **page console** shows the active p

age's own `console.*` output and
uncaught exceptions live, and runs the script you type in it (Enter

s, and a clear button empties it.
- While the Agent drives, the panel **draws the operation**: a tin

ted lock veil
covers the picture (the browser is locked for that moment), a simulated
pointer travel

s to the target and a water ripple marks the click, scrolls get
large arrows fading in the direction

of travel, drags swap the pointer for a
clenched hand, and key presses get a keycap. The drawn curs

or, ripple and
[该节后续省略]
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or from the Harness UI: **Plugins → Add → `@restregular/dsh-visual-browser`**.

Requirements: Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, or Chromium on the machine
(auto-detected), and Node.js

22 or newer (the plugin ships no runtime
dependencies; it talks CDP over the built-in WebSocket).
## Use

1. Open the right Sidebar. Under the built-in **浏览器 / Browser** card sits the
Visual Browser row — c

lick it, or click the **浏览器** card itself and then the
extra row beneath it. The tab opens and repla

ces the guide in that pane.
2. Ask the Agent something that needs a website, for example
*"打开 exampl

e.com 看看首页写了什么"*. The Agent calls `browser_open`.
3. Watch the picture. Click, drag, wheel and type

straight into it. The tab strip
sits above the toolbar; the toolbar below it carries the address box

(type a
URL and press Enter) plus back / forward / reload / **new page** / stop / and
**跟随 / Follow

** — the takeover switch described below. A
tab strip always shows (even with one page): ＋ adds a pa

ge, a chip switches
to it, its × closes it (the last page stays) and the strip falls back to the
tab

on its left — or, when the leftmost page goes, to the one that takes its
place.
The whole rounded c

hip is the hit area — a click anywhere on it (padding,
icon, title) switches pages, and dragging fro

m anywhere on it reorders the
strip (the × keeps its own click and close). Right-click a chip for re

fresh /
copy link / open in your default browser / reference in the chat / close /
close all; the li

fted chip follows the
pointer, slides on frosted glass, and the other chips move aside like
Chrome's

own tab strip. Once the chips outgrow the strip it scrolls sideways,
and its bar floats over the st

rip's bottom edge instead of taking a row of its
own: a thin pill that thickens a little when the po

inter comes near it, and
that you can grab and drag to scroll the strip.
Every page is a real Chrome

tab with its own history;
[该节后续省略]
### What the Agent sees
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Numbers are reassigned on every view, so an action always uses the newest
numbers; a stale one fails

with a clear "take a fresh snapshot" message instead
of clicking the wrong element.
## How it works

- **Host** (`index.js`, `lib/`): launches Chrome with
`--remote-debugging-port=0 --user-data-dir=<pr

ofile>`, parses the DevTools
endpoint from stderr, attaches one flattened CDP session, and exposes:

- five tools through the `tools` service (registration is effect-scoped),
- a same-origin prefix rou

te `/visual-browser/api`:
| Route | Purpose |

| `GET /state` | Status, viewport, tabs and the page console (tiny JSON poll). |
| `GET /stream` | O

ne long response of `[len][seq][jpeg]` frames. |
| `POST /input` | A batch of pointer / wheel / key

/ text events. |
| `POST /page` | new / select / close / reload / close-all / move one page. |
| `PO

ST /console` | eval a script in the active page, or clear the console. |
| `POST /start`, `POST /sto

p`, `POST /nav` | Open a URL, close Chrome, back/forward/reload. |
- **Live picture** (`lib/browser.

js`): `Page.startScreencast` pushes a JPEG per
painted frame; the manager acks each frame and fans t

he same buffer out to every
panel. The first subscriber restarts the screencast so a still page appe

ars at
once; the last one stops it, so a closed panel costs nothing. No screenshot is
taken per clic

k, and nothing about the picture touches the model context.
- **Input** (`lib/browser.js`): panel ev

ents become `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` /
`Input.dispatchKeyEvent` / `Input.insertText` commands. Not

hing waits for a
snapshot or a capture, so input latency is one round trip; the client batches
per a

nimation frame so a drag or flick is one request, not thirty.
- **Snapshot** (`lib/page-scripts.js`)

: one serialized function runs in the page,
filters interactive elements to the viewport, assigns `d

ata-dsh-vb-ref`
numbers, and returns structured JSON. Nothing else about the DOM leaves the
page.
-

**Survives a host restart**: Chrome writes `DevToolsActivePort` into its
profile, so a restarted hos

t (or one whose previous host crashed with Chrome
still alive) attaches to that browser instead of f

ailing on the profile lock.
An adopted browser is only detached — its process is not killed.
Chrome is killed with its process tree when the plugin unloads.
